purpose: Authoritative-provider delta promoting the existing MRPeasy base-catalog target after its August 2026 REST API v2 expansion. This file must override the base record rather than add a duplicate system ID. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, payroll mutation, private-network access or paid services were used.

patch.name: MRPeasy
patch.evidenceNote: Provider-owned MRPeasy documentation confirms HTTPS REST/OpenAPI APIs, Basic HTTP authentication using API key and secret, v1 plus an expanding v2 API, provider-recommended per-resource fallback from v2 to v1, v1 Range/206 pagination, v2 limit/offset pagination, 429 throttling, multi-site identifiers, custom manufacturing-order fields, manufacturing orders/production reports/workstations/routings, inventory, vendors, user action logs and v2 accounting/general-ledger data. August 2026 release notes confirm substantial new v2 endpoints for reports, dashboard data, production resources and stock. Exact API-key authority granularity, tenant/account identity, practical rate limits and complete endpoint parity require an authorised account.
securityEvidenceBlockers: Public documentation establishes an account API key/secret but does not prove a separately scoped read-only API credential. Before authentication evidence advances, prove the effective authority of a dedicated integration credential and denied POST/PUT/DELETE paths.
The same API surface exposes production and commercial mutations. WFM must use an explicit GET/read route allowlist and never infer safety from successful Basic authentication.
MRPeasy v2 is explicitly incomplete and evolving. Version fallback must be resource-specific and provider-declared; 401/403/429/5xx responses must not trigger silent downgrade to v1.

requiredPermissions: use a dedicated API key/secret and keep it executor-boundary-only
pin HTTPS host api.mrpeasy.com and exact reviewed read routes
prove credential rotation/revocation and denied writes before tenant-authenticated evidence
namespace checkpoints by API version and pagination contract
dataAvailableOrExpected: manufacturing orders, production timing, products/BOM/routings, workstations and sites
inventory, lots/serials, stock snapshots, units and product groups
v2 accounting/general-ledger manufacturing material, overhead and labour-cost evidence
read-only user action logs and customer-defined manufacturing-order custom fields
stableIdentifiers: preserve MRPeasy database IDs for orders, products, BOMs, routings, workstations, sites, vendors and transactions
namespace IDs by customer account/connection and site where applicable

freshnessLatency.rest: polling-based and constrained by provider throttling/response size
freshnessLatency.webhooks: no webhook contract relied on; scheduled reads remain completeness mechanism

paginationDeltaEvents.v1: Range request header plus 206 Partial Content
paginationDeltaEvents.delta: object-specific timestamps/filters plus overlap reads and stable-ID dedupe
paginationDeltaEvents.versionTransition: v2 preferred where provider documents coverage; v1 only for declared gaps

rateLimitsAndRetries: 429 requires adaptive bounded retry rather than increased concurrency
401/403 stop blind retry and never trigger API-version downgrade
413 reduces page size without changing semantic checkpoint
large backfills partition by object/site/date window and reconcile overlap
versionsRegionsCustomFields: v1 and v2 differ in route and pagination semantics; API version stays in provenance
preserve site, currency, timezone, locale and units explicitly
custom_<id> fields remain source extensions until mapped
public material does not prove customer-selectable API data residency
automationOpportunities: forecast overtime/agency need from backlog and real-vs-planned production duration joined to WFM skills/availability
avoid assigning paid labour to jobs that cannot run because inventory/BOM material is unavailable
separate supplier-driven schedule risk from labour-driven risk
reconcile manufacturing labour/overhead evidence against authoritative WFM pay cost for labour-per-order/unit
bootstrap production, inventory, supplier and finance dimensions from one cloud source for faster SMB implementation
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time by detecting material-blocked work before labour is assigned
reduce overtime/agency spend by identifying production-capacity gaps earlier
improve costing accuracy by reconciling ERP production-cost evidence with authoritative WFM pay and output
reduce integration maintenance through resource-scoped v1/v2 routing instead of customer-specific forks
causalOutcomeReadiness: preserve account/connection, site, object ID, API version, schema fingerprint, source/effective time and ingestion time
retain competing changes such as material receipts, order priority, routing/workstation and supplier delay when assessing workforce interventions
dataGaps: no authorised tenant available to prove credential scope, real schemas, practical limits, multi-site behaviour or denied writes
no universal modified-since/change-token contract across all objects
customer-selectable API data residency not publicly established

API key/secret authority is potentially broad until tenant evidence proves otherwise
v1/v2 coexistence can mask failures if fallback is not fail-closed
custom fields and separate customer accounts can collide without connection/site/version provenance
